`bulk-insert` and `import csv` preserve that identity. Promote scalar references only after the landed data is ready for an explicit model refactor.

DocumentationNarrative.Body:
Generate a diff from the baseline to the feature workspace, then apply it to the integration workspace:
```powershell meta instance diff .\BaselineWorkspace .\FeatureWorkspace --output-xml .\FeatureWorkspace.instance-diff meta instance merge .\IntegrationWorkspace .\FeatureWorkspace.instance-diff ```
The diff describes instance changes by entity and `Id`; it does not merge model definitions.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: Move instance changes between workspaces

DocumentationNarrative.Body:
Rows are identified by entity and `Id`. `meta instance diff` compares two workspace instance graphs and writes a structured description of added, removed, and changed rows, scalar values, and relationship usages. It is a semantic diff, not a text diff.
`meta instance merge` applies that change artifact to a target workspace after validating its precondition and resulting relationships. The default diff output is the sibling path `<RightWorkspace>.instance-diff`.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: Semantic instance diff and merge

DocumentationNarrative.Body:
Merge validates both identity and referential integrity before it writes. Missing required relationships, missing target rows, deleted rows that remain referenced, and changed target preconditions stop the operation.
The result is either a valid target workspace or no persisted change.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: Merge validation

DocumentationNarrative.Body:
The target workspace and diff artifact are positional arguments:
```powershell meta instance merge .\IntegrationWorkspace .\FeatureWorkspace.instance-diff ```
The command checks that the target still matches the diff precondition, applies the described instance changes, validates the resulting workspace, and publishes it as one operation.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: Applying a diff

DocumentationNarrative.Body: Apply a structured instance diff to a target workspace only when its precondition still matches, so workspace changes synchronize without text merges.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: Summary

DocumentationNarrative.Body:
Equal-model diff and merge use the entity and `Id` identities directly. When the two workspaces have different model contracts, use an explicit alignment workspace:
```powershell meta instance diff-aligned .\BaselineWorkspace .\FeatureWorkspace .\AlignmentWorkspace --output-xml .\FeatureWorkspace.instance-diff meta instance merge-aligned .\IntegrationWorkspace .\FeatureWorkspace.instance-diff ```
The alignment is authored data. It makes the contract difference visible instead of hiding it in a matching heuristic.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: Aligned diff and merge

DocumentationNarrative.Body:
`meta model refactor property-to-relationship` changes a scalar reference into a modeled relationship and rewrites the affected instance data in the same operation.
For a landed `Order.ProductId` field:
```powershell meta model refactor property-to-relationship --source Order.ProductId --target Product --lookup Id ```
The command preserves row identities and removes the scalar property by default. Use `--preserve-property` only when retaining both forms is part of the model contract.

Land the files with stable identities, inspect the exact suggestions, and apply the refactors you accept:
```powershell meta import csv .\demo-csv\products.csv --entity Product --output-xml .\Workspace cd .\Workspace meta import csv ..\demo-csv\suppliers.csv --entity Supplier meta model suggest --print-commands meta model refactor property-to-relationship --source Order.ProductId --target Product --lookup Id ```
Suggestions are printed only when the landed values provide a complete, unambiguous reference.

DocumentationNarrative.Body:
The landing workflow is short:
1. Import CSV rows with stable `Id` values. 2. Run `meta model suggest`. 3. Apply the exact relationship promotions that belong in the model.
The suggestion step uses the landed values and declared model structure. It does not guess a relationship when the reference is incomplete or ambiguous.

DocumentationNarrative.Body:
`meta` is the command line for creating and working with model and instance workspaces. It authors models, edits records, imports external metadata, and changes a workspace between XML, SQL, and C# surfaces.
Use `model` commands for structure, `insert` and `bulk-insert` for records, `instance` commands for existing data, and `import` for external sources. Semantic diff and merge move instance changes between workspaces while preserving entity and record identity.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: Working with meta
